indian.headline: Indian markets ended mixed as Nifty gained 0.48% while Bank Nifty slipped; IPO momentum and NRI inflows drove sentiment.
indian.lead: Indian markets ended mixed as Nifty gained 0.48% while Bank Nifty slipped; IPO momentum and NRI inflows drove sentiment.
indian.brief: Sensex rose 0.11% and Nifty 50 climbed 0.48%, but Bank Nifty fell 0.02%, with pharma (+0.9%) and IT (+0.6%) outperforming banking.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities delivered a mixed close on 25 August 2026, with the broader Nifty 50 gaining 0.48% while the banking index turned slightly negative. Pharma and IT sectors led the charge with gains of 0.9% and 0.6% respectively, signalling resilience in defensive and tech-driven plays. The day was buoyed by strong IPO momentum—Sunshine Pictures debuted with 14% grey market premium gains, while Augmont Enterprises' jewellery IPO saw explosive 14.46x subscription on Day 3 with a 42% grey market premium, reflecting robust retail and institutional appetite for new listings.

Beyond equities, the macro backdrop remained constructive. Foreign currency deposits (FCNR-B) saw strong inflows, with Jefferies forecasting $90–100 billion in total inflows by end-August, exceeding earlier estimates and underscoring NRI confidence in India. Housing price gains (1.1% sequential rise in Q1 FY27), Marriott's expansion plans, and strategic corporate partnerships (Tata Capital-Resona Bank MoU) signalled healthy underlying economic momentum. However, air fares surged 31.9% year-on-year, and raw sugar imports were eased to combat hoarding—twin signals of price pressures in pockets of the economy that warrant monitoring.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: Japan-India partnerships (Resona Bank, localisation push) offset by air price inflation signals.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: No fresh data; strong NRI deposit inflows via FCNR-B channels continue.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Russia pledges uninterrupted energy supplies; no intraday volatility reported.

indian.watch: Tata Sons board meeting on 17 September for Chairman transition clarity; Augmont and Sunshine listing debuts this week.

us.headline: US markets mixed as tech slides, financials rally amid trade tensions and bond yield concerns.
us.lead: US markets mixed as tech slides, financials rally amid trade tensions and bond yield concerns.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.28%, Nasdaq dropped 0.76%, but Dow gained 0.26% as sector rotation continued.
us.narrative:
US markets ended a choppy Tuesday with mixed signals: the tech-heavy Nasdaq tumbled 1.8% while financials gained 1.3%, suggesting traders rotated out of growth stocks into banks. Treasury Secretary Bessent's efforts to lower bond yields faced skepticism from prediction market traders betting yields will keep rising through 2026, adding pressure to rate-sensitive sectors. Energy stocks fell 0.8% amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

Trade war escalation dominated headlines as US-Canada negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods and matching retaliation vows from Ottawa. Ford's $3 billion Canadian manufacturing bet faces fresh uncertainty. Separately, Iran faced sweeping new US sanctions, while crypto rallied 3% to near $80,000 on institutional inflows. In Asia, Infosys cut bonus payouts to 70%, and China's Unitree robot maker slumped 45% post-IPO after a 460% debut spike.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Sharp rotation as bond yield concerns weigh on growth stocks.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Institutional inflows and short-squeeze liquidations fuel crypto momentum.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: US-Canada tariff escalation and geopolitical tensions create headwinds.

us.watch: Monitor whether US-Canada tariff war spreads to other nations and impacts supply chains tomorrow.
